LESSON: READING 8.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: VISUALS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we say a picture is worth a thousand words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify information from visuals for information

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify information from visuals for information
   In simple words: practise until you can identify information from visuals for information. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals.
4. Show that you can: identify information from visuals for information

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Work jointly to study a visual related to the theme and discuss with peers,
2. Work jointly to summarise a text using a visual e.g. pictures, graphs, charts, mind maps,
3. Display the visual on charts for peer review,
4. Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner prepares a mosaic piece using available materials on an idea related to the theme on technology.
5. Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner shows defining personal skills when summarising a text using visuals e.g. pictures, graphs, charts, mind maps. 46 Values:

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify information from visuals for information

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
